A Photograph as Historical Evidence

Remembering football team “Trikki” through family and community

01 / The object

A single photograph as historical evidence

What can a football photograph tell us about a community?

The photograph at the centre of Maria Christakou’s project is part of a family archive in Trikala, Greece. Showing members of the local football club Trikki in the 1950s, it becomes a point of departure for reconstructing neighbourhood relationships, amateur sport and the ways memories circulate between families and public history.

The people in the image are not all individually identified by the submitted document. The photograph therefore offers evidence of the team’s public presence without providing a complete account of every player’s life.

02 / Forming a team

Football in the neighbourhoods of Trikala

By 1947, three football clubs were active in Trikala: Achilleus, led by Vasileios Katafigiotis and associated with blue and white; PAOT, associated with yellow and black; and Heracles, associated with green and white. According to the submitted essay, Trikki was informally founded in 1949 by young players from neighbourhoods including Saraya, Tabakika, Kallithea, Gardikaki, Kosmali, Stathmos, Trana Mnimata, Kyrna and Flegiou.

The new team adopted green and white. Players purchased their own uniforms, and changing rooms were arranged first in the basement of general manager Athanasios Christakos’s home on Syngrou Street and later at the home of Georgios Kyritsis, near the stadium on Katsimidou Street. These practical arrangements situate football in ordinary domestic and neighbourhood spaces.

03 / Club history

Recognition, competition and local networks

In spring 1950, PAOT and Heracles merged to establish the Athletic Union of Trikala (AET), whose colours were red and white. The contributor identifies physical education teacher Vasileios Peligos as an important figure in that development.

Trikki received official recognition in 1951 and joined the Thessaly Football Association. Together with the newly established Diagoras, it competed in the Second Division championship. The club’s history is preserved not only through match results but through the names of those who organised, trained and supported the players.

Read the team’s recorded board and coaches, 1951–1960

04 / The people

The names in the records

Christakou’s essay preserves a long list of contracted players and substitutes from 1951 to 1960. Such lists are an important form of community evidence, even when spellings and abbreviations require checking against the original club records.

05 / Voices & remembrance

A player’s story and a team anthem

The submitted photo essay refers to a brief film about a former player, titled in Greek Η ποδοσφαιρική ομάδα “Τρίκκη” Τρικάλων. Its earlier exhibition version provides a link, but the present source PDF does not contain the film or its transcript.

Related film mentioned by the contributor

The external film link is preserved as a separate resource. Availability and permissions are controlled by its host.

Open the linked film ↗

The team anthem, attributed by the author to player Sotirios Gorgogetas (1957–1958), presents the club in the language of local pride:

Trikki is a team with a starting lineup of aces, all brave lads, all fine young men. With Christakos as captain and Miga’s curling shot, the ball flies into the net

These lines are reproduced as a short excerpt from the contributor’s submitted historical material; the original song’s authorship is credited above.

06 / Public memory

From the family album to the newspaper

A newspaper retrospective published more than fifty years after the events brought Trikki back into the local public record. The article reproduces historical team photographs and recalls the club’s beginnings. For Christakou, that later act of publication shows how a family-held image can be read alongside a community’s broader memory.

Curatorial note

A family photograph and a newspaper retrospective have different evidential limits. The first preserves a specific image in family custody; the second demonstrates how the club was publicly narrated later. The complete bibliographic details and reproduction permissions for the newspaper are not provided in the submission.

07 / Reflection

What remains when the players are gone?

The project closes with a question about the survival of personal and collective memory. The photograph does not tell the whole history of Trikki, yet it opens a path from names and faces to the relationships, neighbourhoods and shared memories that made the club possible.

As Christakou concludes, what remains when people and moments are gone are the memories that continue to give life meaning.
